caption: Job longs for someone to stand between him and God; First Timothy calls Jesus the mediator. The parallel is meaningful, but Job voices a wish—not a prediction.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Job predict Jesus as mediator? Job wishes someone could stand between him and God. First Timothy later calls Jesus the one mediator.
slides.body: Job wishes someone could stand between him and God. First Timothy later calls Jesus the one mediator.
slides.heading: Did Job predict Jesus as mediator?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Job 9:32-33: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
slides.body: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
slides.heading: Job 9:32-33

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in 1 Tim 2:5, BSB: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
slides.body: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · 1 Tim 2:5

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The comparison feels natural Jesus fills the role Job longs for: someone able to bring God and humanity together.
slides.body: Jesus fills the role Job longs for: someone able to bring God and humanity together.
slides.heading: The comparison feels natural

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Job is expressing a wish He does not predict a future person. The words for Job’s imagined arbiter and Timothy’s mediator are different.
slides.body: He does not predict a future person. The words for Job’s imagined arbiter and Timothy’s mediator are different.
slides.heading: But Job is expressing a wish

title: Job's missing mediator
